newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Germany confident on stab pact by end-June - source.
newsitem.headline: Germany confident on stab pact by end-June - source.

text.p: Germany is confident that European nations can agree by the end of June on a stability pact on lasting fiscal discipline on European monetary union, a source close to the German delegation said on Monday.
"Of that I am confident," said the source, who asked not to be identified.
He added that the pact could not be finally agreed at the Amsterdam summit on June 16-17 because the French government did not yet have a final position on the pact.
"The markets had expected a deal in Amsterdam. Now they will have to wait a bit." He added he hoped markets would realise such a delay is normal given the new government in France.

"The orientation of the stability pact has not been called into question," the source said, adding that German acceptance of any French demands for elements of employment policy to be added depended "on how far they go."
The source said Germany agreed on the need for better coordination on economic and fiscal policies.
"But we are against an economic government because that would affect the independence of the central bank."
The documentation of the stability pact would in any case not have been ready until after the Amsterdam summit, the source said.
